query: Casting is the predominant fabrication method for high-entropy alloys, but solidification-related porosity and microstructural nonuniformity can cause heterogeneous properties. Studies of other high-entropy-alloy compositions have reported high hardness and notable compressive performance, yet these findings do not establish how to improve CoCrFeNiTi; moreover, some investigated alloys were brittle at 25 °C and displayed only limited plastic deformation at 600 °C. For equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi with a simple crystal structure, favorable plasticity and machinability, but low hardness and load-bearing capability, what single intervention could improve hardness and mechanical performance while preserving those favorable characteristics and clarifying the relationship between microstructure and deformation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, a quantitative prediction relative to the unmodified alloy, the processing and testing boundaries within which it should apply, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled microstructural and mechanical experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Nb to CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy will improve its hardness and mechanical performance while preserving favorable plasticity and machinability.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi with a simple crystal structure
generation.conditions: High-energy ball milling and discharge plasma sintering
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of Laves phase (Co2Nb-type, HCP) and lattice distortion in the FCC matrix
generation.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening and precipitation strengthening due to the formation of hard, brittle Laves phase
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved hardness (e.g., > 300 HV) and mechanical performance (e.g., tensile strength > 800 MPa) while maintaining favorable plasticity (e.g., elongation > 30%)
generation.boundary: Nb content between 0-9 wt%, sintering temperature between 1000-1200 °C
generation.uncertainty: Optimal Nb content and processing conditions for achieving the best balance of properties

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of mechanical properties and microstructure of CoCrFeNiTi alloys with and without Nb addition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Nb does not result in improved hardness and mechanical performance while maintaining favorable plasticity, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does doping with different Nb contents (0–9 wt%) affect the microstructure, mechanical properties, and fracture behavior of CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys prepared by high-energy ball milling and discharge plasma sintering?. System: CoCrFeNi-Nbx (x = 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 wt%) high-entropy alloys. Processing: High-energy ball milling (400 rpm, 4 h total with 10 min cooling intervals) followed by discharge plasma sintering (SPS) at 1100 °C, 30 MPa pressure, for 10 min; heating rates: 100 °C/min (0–600 °C), 50 °C/min (600–900 °C), 25 °C/min (900–1100 °C). Test conditions: Room temperature tensile testing (cross-sectional area 1.5 mm × 1 mm, tensile rate 0.2 mm/min, original gauge length 5 mm); Vickers hardness (500 g load, 15 s retention); XRD (Cu Kα, 40 kV, 40 mA, 20–90°); SEM/EDS analysis.
